title: uml-mcp: ask your assistant for a diagram

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You type a sentence in chat, and a clean sequence diagram appears. That's what Antoine's open source project, uml-mcp, makes possible.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How does the assistant draw diagrams?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Through MCP, the Model Context Protocol, which lets an assistant call real tools. uml-mcp is a server with diagram tools: the assistant writes the diagram source in Mermaid, PlantUML or another supported format, and the server sends back a rendered image and useful links.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Think of the assistant as an architect and uml-mcp as the printing shop.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Perfect picture. The architect hands over a sketch in text form, and the shop returns the blueprint.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Five documented tools: generate a diagram, generate an image, validate the source, list the available diagram types, and render several at once. Through Kroki it covers around thirty-seven types.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do the editable links work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For Mermaid, the code builds a small JSON state, compresses it with zlib and encodes it in URL-safe base64. That one state powers both an image link and an editable mermaid dot live link. It also picks the right endpoint for SVG versus PNG, JPEG or WebP.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why MCP rather than the earlier tools?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine started with a ChatGPT diagram plugin and AIPRM sequence templates. Both work, but he wanted native tools: enable a server once, call generate UML from the agent, and save the Mermaid file and SVG beside a blog post. MCP is that layer. The plugin idea is the same, but the host is different.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do you set it up in Cursor?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Install from the GitHub repository, add the server to Cursor's MCP settings, then ask for a specific type, like a Mermaid sequence with a user, React, FastAPI and Postgres. There's also a hosted endpoint and a docs site.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: An admin command, metrics, and a Kroki playground that make it easy to see what the renderer is doing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine uses it across his blog for pipeline and career diagrams. The full post has a sequence diagram of the flow and links to the project page.
